features.name: First launch, no account
features.what: A fresh Mac opens to an empty chat: the frog on its lily pad, 'What should we work on?', recent-project chips, and a sidebar footer offering Frog Cloud sign-in. Nothing needs an account.
entry_points: Launch Frog.app for the first time
File > New Chat (⌘N) or a new window

flows.name: Open the app for the first time with no account
steps: Launch Frog with an empty HOME and no Frog Cloud key
Look at the window that opens
flows.expected: One window with an empty chat: frog mascot, 'What should we work on?', composer. The footer reads 'Sign in to Frog Cloud · Cloud sessions · $1 free to start'.
flows.why_hard: The app-level launch (RootView, WindowGroup, UserFooter reading CloudAccount.shared) has no test entry point. Only EmptyTranscript is rendered, as a PNG with no reference compare. SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.name: Jump into a recent project from the empty chat
steps: Have git repos under ~/Developer (or recent folders)
Click one of up to three folder chips
flows.expected: The window switches to a new conversation in that folder (hand-off to the shell's folder switch).
flows.why_hard: RecentProjectChips reads Library.shared, Recents and the real home folder, and the click goes through the switchFolder environment closure. SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.name: Start from a suggested prompt in a project
steps: Open a project folder with no conversation yet
Click a start chip like 'Review my changes'
flows.expected: Summary such as 'Rust and Swift · 41k lines · 3 uncommitted changes'. Clicking a chip submits its prompt as the first message (hand-off to the conversation).

features.name: Apple Intelligence as the first model
features.what: With nothing set up, new conversations start on Apple's on-device model (apple/on-device through the frog-apple sidecar), so the first message gets an answer with no download or account.
entry_points: Send the first message in a new chat on a Mac with Apple Intelligence on

flows.name: Get a first answer with no setup
steps: Fresh HOME, Apple Intelligence enabled in System Settings
Type a question in a new chat
flows.expected: The turn shows 'Starting Apple Intelligence', then streams an answer. The model pill reads Apple Intelligence. Hand-off to the conversation for the transcript itself.
flows.why_hard: It needs the real frog-apple sidecar and a Mac with Apple Intelligence available. Test hosts run with FROG_SIDECARS=off, and CI VMs have no Apple Intelligence. A stand-in model (HeldModel) can replace it for the flow but not for the Apple path.

flows.name: Open a first chat on a Mac without Apple Intelligence
steps: Look at the model pill and the empty page
flows.expected: No Apple model is offered. The model suggestion line offers the local model that suits this Mac, and the picker offers Frog Cloud.
flows.why_hard: AppleIntelligence.available reads SystemLanguageModel.default directly, with no seam to force it on or off.

features.name: First download offer (model suggestion)
features.what: While there's no model on this Mac and no cloud key, the empty page offers one quiet line: 'Using Apple Intelligence. Get Qwen3 32B for bigger tasks · 18 GB', with the model picked by this Mac's memory.
entry_points: Empty conversation page, under the question

flows.name: See which model Frog recommends for this Mac
steps: Fresh Mac with no local model and no cloud key
flows.expected: It offers Qwen3 32B (18 GB) at 48 GB of RAM or more, Qwen3 8B at 16 GB or more, else Qwen3 4B, sized as Settings writes it.
flows.why_hard: SuggestedModel.forThisMac reads ModelIdentity.memoryGB from the real machine, so the RAM tiers can't be injected. ModelSuggestion reads ModelDownloads.shared and ProviderStore.shared (which runs the real `frog --providers`).

flows.name: Download the suggested model from the empty page
steps: Open a new chat on a fresh Mac
Watch the line change to 'Downloading … · progress' with a Stop link
Wait for the download to finish
flows.expected: Progress shows in place. When done, the new chat switches to the model, flashes '<model> is ready on this Mac.', and lastModel is remembered. The line goes away.
flows.why_hard: ModelDownloads always fetches from https://huggingface.co (multi-GB). There's no URL or session seam, and the view isn't clickable in tests.

flows.name: Stop the download started from the suggestion line
steps: Open a new chat on a fresh Mac
flows.expected: The download is cancelled, partial state cleared, and the line goes back to offering Get.
flows.why_hard: It needs a real download in flight (no fake downloader). SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.name: Turn the model suggestion off for good
steps: Open a new chat with the suggestion showing
Click the × at the end of the line
flows.expected: The line is gone and stays gone (modelSuggestionClosed = true).
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.name: No suggestion once a model or cloud key exists
steps: Download a catalog model or connect a cloud key
flows.expected: The suggestion line doesn't appear.
flows.why_hard: hasCloud comes from ProviderStore.shared.load(), which runs the real `frog --providers --json`. hasLocal reads the real HF cache (only HF_HUB_CACHE can redirect it).

features.name: Found Claude Code setup line
features.what: On an empty page, frog says what it found from Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, skills, keys) and offers to add Claude Code's MCP servers with one click.
entry_points: Empty conversation page, while `frog --setup` reports MCP servers to add

flows.name: Use the MCP servers found in Claude Code
steps: Read 'Using your Claude Code setup: … Found N MCP servers.'
flows.expected: It runs `frog --use-claude-mcp on`. The line becomes 'Using N MCP servers from Claude Code.' with a check, and an empty conversation restarts so the servers connect.
flows.why_hard: It needs the real engine to report and enable servers (no stub for Frog.json/Frog.run). SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.name: Hide the setup line
steps: Have Claude Code MCP servers frog could add
Open a new chat with the setup line showing
flows.expected: The line is gone for good (setupLineClosed), and the model suggestion takes its place.
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

features.name: Bigger model offer
features.what: When a small model (Apple Intelligence's 8k window) outgrows the conversation, loops or works in a project, a line above the composer offers the next model up on your devices or in the cloud. Hand-off: it sits in the composer area.
entry_points: Above the composer after a turn ends on a small-window model

flows.name: Move a struggling conversation to a bigger local model
steps: Chat on Apple Intelligence until a turn ends on context overflow or looping
flows.expected: A ready model takes over the conversation now. A Get downloads and switches when ready (Workspace.useWhenReady).
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree). The Get path needs a real download.

flows.name: Move to a cloud model, or to Frog Cloud setup
steps: Chat on a small model until the bigger-model line shows
Click 'use <cloud model>' (or 'use Frog Cloud' when none is ready)
Look at the model pill or the Settings window
flows.expected: A ready cloud model takes over (or the folder's keep-on-device policy asks first). With none ready, Settings opens on the Models tab.
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree). openSettings can't be observed in a test host.

flows.name: Keep the small model
steps: Chat on a small model until the bigger-model line shows
flows.expected: The line goes away for this conversation.
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

features.name: Settings window and tabs
features.what: ⌘, opens a nine-tab Settings window (General, Models, Billing, Energy, Lend, Permissions, MCP, Appearance, Shortcuts). The last tab is remembered, and other surfaces deep-link to a tab through the settingsTab default.
entry_points: Sidebar footer when signed in (opens Billing)
Picker or model row 'Raise Cap…' (Models or Billing)

flows.name: Open Settings and switch tabs
flows.expected: Settings opens 620 pt wide on the last tab used, and each tab's content loads.
flows.why_hard: The Settings scene can't be opened or its tabs clicked from a hosted test. Several tabs run the real engine on appear (MCP, Models through Devices).

flows.name: Open Settings straight onto a tab from elsewhere
flows.expected: settingsTab is set first, so Settings opens (or switches) to the right tab.
flows.why_hard: openSettings() can't be observed in a test host. The tab binding itself (UserDefaults 'settingsTab') could be asserted.

features.name: Open files in (editor)
features.what: Settings › General picks the app that opens files: Automatic (first installed editor) or a specific installed editor.

flows.name: Choose which editor opens files
steps: Pick an editor from 'Open files in'
Open a file from a conversation or 'Open config.toml…'
flows.expected: The chosen editor opens the file. Automatic uses the first installed editor, or the default app.
flows.why_hard: Editor.installed depends on the apps installed on the Mac, and Editor.open launches real apps. SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

features.name: Notifications and the Dock badge
features.what: frog notifies only when the model's Notify tool asks (attention, done, silent), posts permission requests with Allow and Deny actions while in the background, and badges the Dock for turns that finished while you were away. The first long turn asks once whether to ping you.
entry_points: Settings › General 'Let frog notify me when I'm in another app'
Ping line above the composer after 30 s of work

flows.name: Turn notifications on or off
steps: Turn off 'Let frog notify me when I'm in another app'
Run a turn where the model calls Notify while frog is in the background
flows.expected: Off: the Notify shows only as a transcript row, with no banner and no Dock bounce. On: a banner.
flows.why_hard: Notifier.note is a no-op under SingleInstance.isTesting, so delivery can't be observed in the test host. The toggle isn't clickable.

flows.name: Get notified by the model at the right loudness
steps: Turn on notifications and switch to another app
Let a turn send notify with urgency attention
Then one with done, then one with silent
flows.expected: attention: time-sensitive banner with sound and one Dock bounce. done: quiet banner. silent: nothing outside the transcript. A finished turn alone never alerts.
flows.why_hard: The tests stop at Conversation.effects. Actual UNUserNotificationCenter delivery needs a signed bundle with notification authorization, which a test host lacks.

flows.name: Allow or deny a permission request from Notification Center
steps: Start a turn that needs permission
In the banner choose Allow (or Deny)
flows.expected: The waiting turn continues (or the step is denied), the banner is removed, and the badge count drops.
flows.why_hard: Needs real Notification Center interaction with a signed, authorized app. needsPermission is skipped under isTesting. The delegate's handler could be called directly as a partial test.

flows.name: See what finished while you were away
steps: Switch to another app until it finishes
flows.expected: A badge appears on the Dock icon and clears when frog becomes active.
flows.why_hard: turnFinishedAway is skipped under isTesting, and inBackground needs the app inactive.

flows.name: Answer 'Ping you when it's done?'
steps: Start a turn that runs longer than 30 s, with notifications not yet decided
See 'This is taking a while. Ping you when it's done?'
flows.expected: Yes asks the system for permission and keeps notifyWhenDone on. No thanks turns it off. Either way it never asks again (pingAsked).
flows.why_hard: Notifier.notAskedYet returns false in test hosts, so the line never shows. The system authorization prompt can't be automated. There's a real 30 s timer and no clock seam.

flows.name: Prove notifications deliver on this build
steps: Build and sign a Debug app with notifications allowed
Choose Debug > Test Notifications (or launch with --test-notification)
Watch Notification Center and the log
flows.expected: One notification of every category is posted, and the system's authorization answer is logged.
flows.why_hard: Needs a real, signed app with notification permission and a visible screen.

features.name: Default model for new chats and messages
features.what: 'New messages use: last model in this chat / a fixed default' and 'New conversations use', in ModelSettings. Present in code but not reachable in v0.7.0.

flows.name: Make every new chat start on one model
steps: Set 'New messages use' to 'A fixed default model'
Pick a ready model in 'New conversations use'
flows.expected: New chats and messages use the chosen model.
flows.why_hard: Not reachable in v0.7.0: ModelSettings (SettingsView.swift) isn't mounted in SettingsView's TabView (the Models tab shows MachinesSettings), and ModelSections.providersHidden = true also hides the entry point. Only a render test hosts it directly. The defaults logic behind it is unit-tested in ModelStatsTests.testNewConversationsStartOnAppleThenTheLastPick, but no user flow reaches it.

features.name: Shortcuts tab
features.what: A read-only list of keyboard shortcuts by group (Conversation, Navigate, Session, Window).

flows.name: Look up a keyboard shortcut
steps: Find a group such as Session
Read the key next to an action
flows.expected: Four groups list the actions with their keys (for example 'New session ⇧⌘N'). The shortcuts themselves belong to the shell agent's area.

features.name: Appearance
features.what: Density, Detail (verbosity), Playful frog, Frog sounds and Show energy use, all app-wide defaults.

flows.name: Make the window denser or roomier
steps: Look at a conversation and the sidebar
flows.expected: Rows and spacing change everywhere at once (density default).
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree). The density key could be set and a render compared, if render tests compared images.

flows.name: Choose how much of the model's work conversations show
steps: Open a conversation with tool calls
flows.expected: The transcript shows more or fewer steps. Conversations with their own Session › Detail keep theirs.
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.name: Turn the playful frog on or off
flows.expected: The empty page shows the plain FrogMark instead of the mascot, and activity words aren't playful.
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.name: Turn frog sounds on
steps: Send a message and let the turn finish
flows.expected: A plip on send, a ribbit on finish, a drip on permission.
flows.why_hard: Audio output can't be observed. SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.name: Show energy use at the end of each turn
flows.expected: Each turn ends with its watt-hours. The Energy tab's toggle mirrors it (same key).
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

features.name: Permissions
features.what: The default permission mode for new sessions (Ask, Accept Edits, Auto, Yolo), the shell sandbox, computer use, and the always-allowed command list in config.toml. Hand-off: the cards these settings produce belong to the conversation.

flows.name: Choose how new sessions ask for permission
steps: Pick Yolo (or Ask / Accept Edits / Auto)
flows.expected: The new session starts with that mode's flag. Resumed sessions keep their own.
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.name: Run shell commands outside the sandbox
steps: Turn off 'Run shell commands in a sandbox'
Start a new session and run a command
flows.expected: The Ask description changes to 'Every edit and command asks first', and new sessions run unsandboxed.
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree). Checking the engine's sandbox state needs the real engine.

flows.name: Let frog see and use other apps
steps: Turn on 'Let frog see and use other apps'
Start a new session and ask it to read another app's window
flows.expected: New sessions can use computer-use tools through Accessibility, asking first.
flows.why_hard: Needs the Accessibility permission granted to the app, a TCC system setting that tests mustn't change.

flows.name: Edit always-allowed commands
flows.expected: ~/.config/frog/config.toml is created with a commented allow_bash example if missing, then opens in the chosen editor.
flows.why_hard: Editor.open launches a real app (no seam). SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree). File creation could be checked in the test HOME.

features.name: MCP servers
features.what: Lists config.toml's MCP servers with their state (connected with N tools, error, signed out or declined, withheld tools), signs in to OAuth servers in the browser, and opens config.toml.

flows.name: Check how each MCP server is doing
flows.expected: Each server shows a green check and its tool count and names, or a red octagon with its error, or a key icon with 'signed out'. Withheld tools are listed with the reason.
flows.why_hard: The list comes from the real `frog --mcp --json` (no Frog.json stub), and the view rows aren't readable in tests. A FROG_BIN stub or a decode test of MCPStatus would cover most of it.

flows.name: Open MCP settings with no servers
flows.expected: 'No servers yet.', plus the example TOML and 'Open config.toml…'.
flows.why_hard: Needs the real engine run, or a stub. SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.name: Sign in to an MCP server that needs OAuth
steps: Configure a URL server that answers 401
Click 'Sign in' on the signed-out row
flows.expected: The row shows a spinner, then reloads by itself with the server connected and its tools listed. Declining leaves 'signed out · you declined'.
flows.why_hard: Runs `frog --mcp-signin`, which opens a real browser OAuth flow against the server. There's no seam for the browser or the server.

flows.name: Edit MCP config and refresh
steps: Click 'Open config.toml…' and add a server
flows.expected: config.toml is created if missing and opens in the editor. Refresh re-reads the list.
flows.why_hard: Editor.open launches a real app, and the list needs the engine. SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

features.name: Models on this Mac
features.what: This Mac's page in Settings › Models lists Frog's picks for its memory, what's already on disk and 'More models'. Each row has one control for its state: Get · size, a progress line and Cancel, Load and Delete, Loading, or Loaded · tok/s and Stop.

flows.name: See the models recommended for this Mac's memory
flows.expected: The best coding model that fits and up to two smaller ones (16 GB: Qwen3 8B, 4B, 1.7B; 64 GB: Qwen3 32B, 14B, 8B). What's on disk always shows. The rest sits behind More models with a count. A note says which models run only in Frog Cloud.

flows.name: Download a model onto this Mac
steps: Watch the progress line with bytes, rate and bar
flows.expected: The row shows download progress, then becomes on disk with Load and Delete. `frog --models` lists it, and the picker offers it.
flows.why_hard: ModelDownloadsTests drives the real store against huggingface.co with a tiny repo and skips offline. The row and button need a real (or stubbed) HF server and a UI driver.

flows.name: Cancel a download in progress
steps: Click Cancel on the progress line
flows.expected: The download stops and the row returns to Get. Already-finished files stay in the cache for a later resume per file.
flows.why_hard: Needs a download in flight (no fake HF server or URLSession seam). SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.name: See why a download failed
steps: Make Hugging Face unreachable (or pick a missing repo)
flows.expected: The row shows the failure reason ('Hugging Face didn't find …') and Get works again as a retry.
flows.why_hard: Forcing the failure needs network control. The row's wording is unit-tested through LocalModelList.build.

flows.name: Load a downloaded model into memory
flows.expected: The row becomes 'Loaded · N tok/s' with Stop, and This Mac's row says what it's running. Past the deadline a stuck load ends with a reason.
flows.why_hard: This Mac's loads go to the real tang sidecar at 127.0.0.1:8911, which is off in test hosts. MockNode could stand in if Devices' local base URL were injectable.

flows.name: Unload the running model
steps: Load a model on This Mac
Click Stop on the loaded row
flows.expected: The model unloads, memory frees, and the row returns to Load. If a turn is running: 'It's busy with a turn. Stop it when it's idle.'
flows.why_hard: Devices.stopModel calls /models/unload, which MockNode doesn't implement, and the local sidecar is off in tests.

flows.name: Delete a model from this Mac
steps: Have a model on disk and not loaded
flows.expected: The cache folder is removed and the row goes back to Get · size. Delete is disabled while loaded ('Stop it first.').
flows.why_hard: The confirmation dialog and buttons can't be clicked in tests. ModelDownloads.remove on a seeded HF_HUB_CACHE could be driven at the store level.

flows.name: See where a model comes from
steps: Click ⓘ next to a model name
flows.expected: A popover with From (a Hugging Face link), Format, Size, Memory and Good for.
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree). Popovers are only rendered directly.

flows.name: See models on disk while the engine isn't running
steps: Put a catalog model in the HF cache
Stop the engine on this Mac
flows.expected: The row reads on disk, and Load is disabled with 'Loads once Frog's engine on this Mac lists it.'

features.name: Models on a paired machine
features.what: On a paired node's page, and from the picker's 'Your machines' rows, load, stop or delete what's on its disk. It says when a model won't fit or the node is busy, and waits for the node's turn to finish before swapping.
entry_points: Model picker › Your machines (hand-off to composer)

flows.name: Load a model on another machine
steps: Click Load on a model that fits
flows.expected: The node loads it and reports Loaded with tok/s. The replaced model goes back to on disk.

flows.name: Try to load a model that doesn't fit
steps: Click Load on a model bigger than its free memory
flows.expected: Nothing is sent when it plainly won't fit. A refused load leaves the row on disk with 'Couldn't load: …' and nothing spinning.

flows.name: Switch a busy node's model
steps: Pair a node and start a turn on it
Pick a different model on that node
flows.expected: One line says it's busy. The swap waits for the turn and happens after, with '<node> switched to …'.

flows.name: Stop the model running on a node
steps: Pair a node with a model loaded
Click Stop on the loaded row
flows.expected: The node unloads it and the row shows Load again. A busy node says to stop it when idle.
flows.why_hard: MockNode has no /models/unload. SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.name: Delete a model from a node's disk
steps: Pair a node with a model on disk
flows.expected: The model is removed (POST /models/delete). An older node shows the button disabled with 'can't delete models. Update it on <node>.'
flows.why_hard: MockNode has no /models/delete. SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.name: Download a model onto a node
steps: Pair a node with a newer tang
flows.expected: Download progress shows on the row. It stalls and fails with reasons from the node. Older nodes say they can't download.
flows.why_hard: LocalModelRowView.get() only acts for This Mac (`guard device.role == .thisMac`), so Get on a node does nothing in v0.7.0 even when enabled. MockNode has no /models/pull.

features.name: Machines in Settings › Models
features.what: Every machine (This Mac first, paired nodes) as one row with its hardware, what it's running with tok/s or idle/offline, and an online dot, plus the Frog Cloud account summary and 'Show cloud models in the picker'.

flows.name: See my machines and what each is running
flows.expected: This Mac and each node, for example 'mew · RTX 3090 · 24 GB VRAM · Qwen3 4B · 58 tok/s'. Offline ones are dimmed, and a fresh Mac says 'not running'.

flows.name: See why machines can't be found
steps: Deny Local Network access to Frog in System Settings
flows.expected: A warning row (devices.browseProblem) explains the browse failure.
flows.why_hard: Needs the Local Network privacy setting changed (TCC), and NWBrowser has no seam.

flows.name: Hide Frog Cloud models from the picker
steps: Turn off 'Show cloud models in the picker'
flows.expected: The Frog Cloud section is gone from the picker (hand-off to the composer's picker).
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree). The ModelMenu.showCloudKey default could be asserted at the model level.

features.name: Pair a machine with a code
features.what: 'Pair a machine…' lists unpaired Frog nodes found on Bonjour. Pair… opens six digit boxes for the code the node shows (from `tang-llm pair`, or a lent Mac's code). Success says '<node> joined your machines.' and closes. The node's fingerprint is pinned.
entry_points: Node offer line above the composer: 'mew is on your network … Use it?'

flows.name: Find machines on my network
steps: Run a Frog node (or MockNode with Bonjour) on the LAN
flows.expected: Unpaired nodes are listed with hardware and a Pair… button. With none: 'No machines found on your network yet.' and the install hint.
flows.why_hard: Devices discovers through NWBrowser (Bonjour), and MockNode isn't fed into Devices' discovery in tests. PairMachineSheet reads Devices.shared.

flows.name: Pair a node by typing its code
steps: In 'Pair a machine…' click Pair… next to it
Type or paste the six digits
flows.expected: The last digit submits. 'Pairing…', then '<node> joined your machines.', and the sheet closes after 1.2 s. The node appears online in Machines, its key goes to the Keychain and nodes.json.
flows.why_hard: PairClient and PairedStore are driven against MockNode, but Devices.pair (which needs a node in Devices.found from Bonjour) and the sheet's digit boxes aren't. Needs a way to inject a found node and drive PairSheet's bindings.

flows.name: Type a wrong code
steps: Open the pair sheet for it
flows.expected: 'That code didn't match. Check it on <node> and try again.' Boxes cleared, focus back on the first box. After five wrong tries the node closes its window and the next try reads '<node> isn't showing a code. Run tang-llm pair on it first.'
flows.why_hard: Covered at PairClient level. The sheet's reset and focus behaviour needs the view driven.

flows.name: Use a code after it expired
steps: Wait out the node's pairing window
flows.expected: '<node> isn't showing a code. Run tang-llm pair on it first.' (PairError.noWindow).

flows.name: Refuse a machine pretending to be the one found
steps: Find a node in 'Pair a machine…'
Have a different machine answer at its address
flows.expected: 'This isn't the <node> Frog found on your network. Nothing was saved.' (PairError.notThatNode).

flows.name: Act on 'mew is on your network. Use it?'
steps: Run an unpaired node on the LAN
Click 'Use it' (pair sheet opens) or 'Not now'
flows.expected: Use it opens the pair sheet for that node. Not now hides the offer for that fingerprint.
flows.why_hard: NodeOffer reads Devices.shared.offer, which needs Bonjour discovery. SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

features.name: A machine's page
features.what: Click a machine for its status, hardware, memory bar and models, and the node controls: share this Mac, rename, unpair.
entry_points: Settings › Models › click a machine row

flows.name: Open a machine's page
steps: Read Status, Hardware and the memory bar
flows.expected: The page is titled with the machine's name, with Status (Idle/Ready/Working, N waiting/Not answering/Stuck loading), hardware and '18 GB of 24 GB used', then its model sections.

flows.name: Rename a machine
steps: Type a new name and press Rename
flows.expected: The name changes in the page title and the Machines list, saved on this Mac only (thisMacName default, or nodes.json for nodes).
flows.why_hard: Devices.rename isn't tested. The alert can't be driven, but the store call could be with a temp PairedStore.

features.name: Pause agents for an update
features.what: An opt-in setting: before Sparkle installs, every engine (open windows and the background fleet) is asked to stop at a safe point within a shared budget (5–120 s, default 20). The resume manifest is written, Sparkle installs and relaunches, and sessions continue with an update note. Off, an update kills engines and they resume as after a crash.
entry_points: Settings › General › 'Pause agents for app updates and resume them' and 'Wait up to Ns'

flows.name: Turn on pausing agents for updates and set the wait
steps: Turn on 'Pause agents for app updates and resume them'
Use the stepper to set 'Wait up to 30s'
flows.expected: The stepper appears only when on, moves in 5 s steps between 5 and 120, and is stored (gracefulUpdates, gracefulUpdateBudget). The footer explains both modes.
flows.why_hard: SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree). UpdateDrain.budget clamping could be unit-tested, but isn't.

flows.name: Update while agents are working, and have them carry on
steps: Start turns in two windows and a background worker
Trigger the update (Sparkle install, or Debug > Simulate Update…)
flows.expected: Each engine gets Drain with the deadline. Ones that miss it are killed. The manifest marks them suspendedByUpdate. After relaunch each continues its turn on the same model with the 'resumed after the app updated' note. Long jobs are listed as stopped.
flows.why_hard: No test calls Updates.drainThenInstall or UpdateDrain.drainAll. It needs live engines (or LiveLinks that answer Drain), and a relaunch, which can't happen inside one test process. The pieces could be tested with stand-in links and a stubbed `immediate` closure.

flows.name: Update with pausing off
flows.expected: Sparkle installs immediately. Engines stop where they are, and turns resume as after a crash on next launch.
flows.why_hard: Needs Sparkle's install path and a relaunch.

It shows a QR code (a frog://pair?name&host&code link the iPhone camera opens in frog) and the 20-character code. New Code signs out every phone. A push relay secret lets the Mac wake the phone through frog.toys.

flows.why_hard: RemoteBridge.shared opens real listeners on fixed ports 8913/8914 and reads the Keychain token, and it's skipped in test hosts. SwiftUI controls in a hosted view can't be found or clicked by tests (no XCUITest target, no accessibility tree)

flows.why_hard: Needs APNs delivery to a real device through the relay. The payload and crypto are unit-tested.

flows.expected: The default browser opens the right URL (frog.toys/?settings=account, ?settings=billing, frog.toys/energy, huggingface.co/<repo>).

features.name: Opening Frog from outside: folders, launch arguments, URLs
features.what: One Frog per build. A second launch hands its -FrogFolder or URL arguments to the running copy and quits. Folders opened from Finder or dropped on the Dock get their own window. The Mac registers no URL scheme in v0.7.0 (no CFBundleURLTypes): frog://pair is only produced, as a QR for the iPhone. Sign-in returns to a 127.0.0.1 listener, and frog-auth:// appears only in docs/design/accounts-ux.md.
entry_points: Finder: open a folder with Frog / drop on the Dock icon

flows.name: Open a folder in Frog from Finder or the Dock
steps: In Finder, drop a folder on the Dock icon (or Open With Frog)
flows.expected: A new window opens on that folder.
flows.why_hard: application(_:open:) needs a real Apple Event from Finder. FolderOpener.open could be called directly, but opening a window breaks the background rule unless it's ordered in hidden.

flows.name: Launch Frog on a folder from the command line
flows.expected: The first window opens on that folder.
flows.why_hard: It's an app launch, and there's no UI-test target to launch the app with arguments.

flows.name: Launch Frog again while it's running
steps: Look at the running copy and the process list
flows.expected: The running copy opens the folder in a window and comes forward, and the second process exits. A different build (Debug vs installed) runs alongside. A hung holder gets an alert naming its pid.
flows.why_hard: The decision logic is unit-tested. The real two-process hand-off over DistributedNotificationCenter needs two app launches.

flows.name: Open a frog:// link on the Mac
steps: Click a frog://… link on the Mac (for example frog://pair?… from the QR)
flows.expected: Nothing in v0.7.0: no scheme is registered, so macOS doesn't route it to Frog. A URL passed as a launch argument reaches the running copy, but application(_:open:) opens only directories.
flows.why_hard: The feature doesn't exist on the Mac at v0.7.0. Only iOS handles frog://pair (apps/ios/Frog/FrogApp.swift onOpenURL).
